mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_HELM + i from HelmMale{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 139), so file 07 is index 6, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Scale Helm. mu.db agrees: group 7 index 6, Player/HelmMale07.bmd.
why_this_one: Martin's and Harold's +3 line, and the third of their four sets. The wandering merchants stock all five Scale pieces at +3, so five of their lines were dropped by Realm.Shelf for want of a row. See shared/Market.Wandering.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 1, 0 - the Dark Knight alone. A hundred and ten strength and no agility, where the Bronze set asked for eighty and twenty.

sheet_from: Data/Player/head_08.OZJ (64x64), skin_barbarian_01.OZJ (256x256) and hide.jpg, from MuMain. The .bmd names head_08.jpg, skin_barbarian_01.jpg and hide.jpg; 110 of the 145 triangles are on the first, 27 on the skin and 8 on hide.
sheet_note:
head_08 is a full helm with a visor: a smooth dark hood over the crown and a face plate whose eyes are painted a bright green, drawn once large and once small on the same page. Mean (69, 86, 79) at chroma 17.

The green eyes are paint and nothing else. MU has a RenderEye for glowing eyes and it is used on monsters - the Elite Bull Fighter's, gated on c->Level == 1 - and there is no such call for a player's helm anywhere in ZzzCharacter. So they are drawn bright on the sheet and shipped bright, which is what the client does.

It carries its own face: 27 triangles of skin_barbarian_01, the same count the Leather Helm has, and that is the other half of the keeps_head rule. Helm index 6 is not in SetCharacterScale's condition and does not need to be, because the face is already inside the model. hide is MU capping the openings, a solid black square, as on ArmorMale10. The set is a dark blue-green metal and every sheet agrees: chroma 17 to 19 about means near (50, 65, 55), which is a verdigris cast on a dark plate rather than the grey of the Plate set or the yellow-brown of the Bronze. It is the darkest metal set built so far - lum 54 on the legs against the Plate set's 137 - and that is worth stating because a dark albedo at metallic 1.0 is the shape of the fault the Bone set had. Here it is not a fault: the Bone set was hide and skull declared metal, and this really is plate. See materials/bone.json for the case that was wrong.
material_note:
Two islands and two answers. Island 0 is 118 triangles - head_08's 110 and hide's 8, the hood and the visor welded into one shell - and takes plate_steel, the profile's default, and the sheets do not argue with it: the colour is a verdigris cast at chroma 18 and the surface is banded plate. A metal's albedo is its reflectance, so a dark blue-green sheet at metallic 1.0 renders as dark blue-green metal - which is the same arithmetic the Bronze set records from the warm end.

Island 1 is 27 triangles, which is skin_barbarian_01's 27 exactly: the face inside the visor, and it takes skin. The count is the same 27 the Leather Helm carries, and it is the other half of the keeps_head rule - helm index 6 is not in SetCharacterScale's condition because it does not need to be, the face being already inside the model.

The bright green eyes are paint. They sit inside island 0 with the rest of the visor and nothing here makes them emit: MU has a RenderEye for glowing eyes and uses it on monsters, never on a player's helm.
material_overrides_why:
plate_steel at 0.55 rather than its own 0.34, because this set is corroded and that figure is for polished plate. The assignment is right and the note above argues it well - a dark blue-green sheet at metallic 1.0 is dark blue-green metal - but the same sheets describe a verdigris cast, and verdigris is corrosion. A patina is the one thing a polished surface is not, and at 0.34 the set came back glassy: broad wet highlights sliding over the cuirass and the greaves with the scrollwork lost under them. Swept in Blender on the assembled set under the rig from MU2/lighting.json at 0.34, 0.48 and 0.60 - by 0.60 the scale pattern and the hip scrollwork read clearly and it looks aged rather than wet, and 0.55 keeps a little more metal in it.

Scoped to this set rather than moved in the library: the Plate set is clean steel and wants the polish it has.
